newsitem.title: JAPAN: Weak yen 'neutral' on Japan trade balance - MOF.
newsitem.headline: Weak yen 'neutral' on Japan trade balance - MOF.

text.p: The weak yen is not having any major impact on Japan's trade balance, and Japan's trade surplus is continuing its declining trend, a Ministry of Finance official said on Monday.
"Japan's trade surplus continues its declining trend... The weak yen is not causing any major effects," the MOF official told reporters.

Japan's huge current account surplus plunged 35.3 percent in the six months to September, compared with the year earlier period, confirming that the declining trend is still in place despite the weaker yen, official data showed on Monday.
In dollar terms, the trade balance changes as the yen weakens, but when converted to yen, the impact of currency fluctuations turns out to be neutral, the official said.
Recent hearings conducted by the finance ministry show that companies are not planning to change the ratio of overseas and domestic production due to the weak yen, the official said.
